1. System Architecture & Platform Capabilities

⚡ Multi-Language Code Practice Lab

Interactive sandbox supporting Python 3, Java, C++, C, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust. Features as-you-type AST syntax diagnostics, delimiter checking, and compiler emulation.

🎓 Interactive Learning Academy

Structured course platform with 7 deep-dive tracks, 25+ interactive lessons, module syllabi, real-time knowledge check quizzes, streak/XP tracking, and digital completion certificates.

🤖 AI Error Concept Explainer

4-tab dynamic diagnostic engine: (1) Root-cause diagnosis, (2) Architectural mental model & real-world analogy, (3) Surgical fix comparison with progressive hints, and (4) Pedagogical AI Tutor chat.

🛡️ Disposable Sandbox Execution

Isolated filesystem runner with strict path traversal assertion, command execution allowlisting (blocking dangerous shell operators), secret token redaction, and multi-language compilers.

34 type: 'concept',
35 summary: 'How JavaScript manages function calls using a LIFO stack, and what a stack trace actually represents.',
36 content: [
37 'When your JavaScript code executes, the JavaScript engine (like Chrome V8 or Node.js) allocates a **Call Stack**. The Call Stack is a single-threaded Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) data structure that tracks where the program currently is in execution.',
38 'Whenever a function is invoked, an **Execution Context** is pushed onto the stack. When the function returns, its frame is popped off.',
39 'When an uncaught error occurs, the engine freezes the current state and dumps the **Stack Trace**. Reading a stack trace from top to bottom reveals the exact call chain that led to the crash: the top line is where the error exploded, and the lines below show the functions that called it.',
40 ],
41 keyTakeaways: [
42 'The Call Stack is single-threaded: only one function executes at any given millisecond.',
43 'A Stack Trace reads bottom-to-top for invocation order, and top-to-bottom for the point of failure.',
44 'Infinite recursion without a base case causes a RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.',
45 ],
46 codeExample: {

50 // Line 2: At top of stack
51 return a * b;
52}
53
54function calculateTotal(price, tax) {
55 // Line 7: Pushes multiply() to the stack
56 return multiply(price, 1 + tax);
57}
58
59// Line 11: Main script starts

83 content: [
84 'One of the most confusing errors for developers is: `ReferenceError: Cannot access variable before initialization`.',
85 'Both `var`, `let`, and `const` are hoisted during the creation phase of an execution context. However, while `var` is initialized immediately with `undefined`, `let` and `const` remain in an uninitialized state called the **Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)**.',

129 title: '2.1 Why `Cannot read properties of undefined` Happens in V8',
130 durationMinutes: 12,
131 type: 'concept',
132 summary: 'Understand the V8 internal property lookup mechanism and why accessing properties on null/undefined is prohibited.',
133 content: [
134 'In JavaScript, primitives like numbers and strings have object wrappers (`Number.prototype`, `String.prototype`) that allow property access. But `null` and `undefined` do not have a prototype.',
135 'When the V8 engine evaluates `obj.user.address.street`, it walks down the chain:',
136 '1. Looks up `obj` -> Found object.',
137 '2. Looks up `.user` on `obj` -> Returns `undefined`.',
138 '3. Tries to look up `.address` on `undefined` -> V8 halts: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "address")`.',
139 'This is because `undefined` has no internal `[[Get]]` slot or prototype table.',
140 ],
141 keyTakeaways: [
142 'null represents intentional absence of value; undefined represents uninitialized variable.',
143 'Neither null nor undefined have a prototype or properties.',
144 'Chained property lookups without defensive guards are the #1 source of web app crashes.',
145 ],

147 language: 'javascript',

176 type: 'interactive_lab',
177 summary: 'Modern syntactic features that make code crash-proof against null/undefined, and how they differ from logical OR (||).',
178 content: [
179 'Prior to ECMAScript 2020, developers had to write verbose nested guards: `if (user && user.profile && user.profile.tier)`.',
180 'Modern JavaScript provides **Optional Chaining (`?.`)**:',
181 '`const tier = user?.profile?.tier;`',
182 'If any reference before `?.` is `null` or `undefined`, the expression short-circuits and safely returns `undefined` instead of throwing an error.',
183 'Combine this with **Nullish Coalescing (`??`)** to provide safe fallbacks without the pitfalls of `||` (which misinterprets valid values like `0` or `""` as falsey).',

187 '`??` checks only for null or undefined, preserving valid falsey values like 0, false, and empty strings.',

224 title: '3.1 The Microtask Queue & Unhandled Promise Rejections',
225 durationMinutes: 14,
226 type: 'interactive_lab',
227 summary: 'Why unhandled promise rejections can terminate Node.js servers and freeze React components.',
228 content: [
229 'Promises run in the **Microtask Queue**, which is processed immediately after the current synchronous script completes and before any rendering or macrotasks (like `setTimeout`).',
230 'If a Promise rejects and there is no `.catch()` handler or surrounding `try...catch` in an `async` function, an `unhandledrejection` event is fired.',
231 'In Node.js >= 15, unhandled promise rejections automatically terminate the process with exit code 1 to prevent corrupt state. In frontend browsers, they lead to silent UI freezes.',
232 ],
233 keyTakeaways: [
234 'Always wrap `await` calls in `try...catch` blocks or chain `.catch()`.',
235 'Never leave a fire-and-forget promise without error handling.',
236 'Use `Promise.allSettled()` instead of `Promise.all()` when you want partial successes.',

440 content: [
441 'JSON Web Tokens (JWT) consist of 3 parts separated by dots: `Header.Payload.Signature`.',

941 id: 'async-unhandled-rejection',
942 title: 'UnhandledPromiseRejection: Network request failed',
943 difficulty: 'Medium',
944 language: 'javascript',
945 category: 'Async & Promises',
946 description:
947 'An asynchronous data loader makes an API request that can reject. Because it lacks a try...catch or error boundary, the promise rejection is unhandled and halts execution. Implement proper async error recovery.',
948 errorNameTarget: 'UnhandledPromiseRejection: Failed to fetch user profile: Network Timeout',
949 relatedCourseId: 'js-ts-debugging',
950 relatedLessonId: 'l5-unhandled-rejections',
951 initialCode: `// Challenge: Handle asynchronous Promise rejections gracefully
952async function fetchUserMetrics(userId) {
953 const simulatedNetworkCall = () =>
954 new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
955 // Simulating a failed network timeout
956 reject(new Error('Network Timeout: Gateway 504'));
957 });
958
959 // 💥 BUG: Awaiting a rejecting promise without a try...catch wrapper!
960 const data = await simulatedNetworkCall();
961 return { status: 200, data };
962}
963
964fetchUserMetrics('usr_102');
965`,
966 solutionCode: `// Challenge: Handle asynchronous Promise rejections gracefully
967async function fetchUserMetrics(userId) {
968 const simulatedNetworkCall = () =>
969 new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
970 reject(new Error('Network Timeout: Gateway 504'));
971 });
972
973 // ✅ FIXED: Enclosed in try...catch to return a graceful fallback
974 try {
975 const data = await simulatedNetworkCall();
976 return { status: 200, data };
977 } catch (error) {
978 console.warn(\`Handled async failure for user \${userId}:\`, error.message);
979 return { status: 504, data: null, error: error.message, isFallback: true };
980 }
981}
982
983fetchUserMetrics('usr_102').then(res => console.log('Recovered result:', res));
984`,
985 hints: [
986 'Wrap the `await simulatedNetworkCall()` in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block.',
987 'In the `catch` block, return a fallback object with `{ status: 504, error: error.message, isFallback: true }` so the caller can handle the outage cleanly.',
988 ],

1108 relatedCourseId: 'react-state-traps',
1109 relatedLessonId: 'l10-mutation-trap',
1110 initialCode: `// Challenge: Fix React Direct State Mutation Bug
1111function addNotification(state, newNotification) {
1112 // 💥 BUG: Direct mutation with .push() retains the same memory reference!
1113 // React's shallow comparison Object.is(oldState, newState) evaluates to TRUE,
1114 // causing React to skip re-rendering the UI.
1115 state.notifications.push(newNotification);
1116 return state;
1117}
1118
1119const currentState = { notifications: ['Welcome!'] };
1120const nextState = addNotification(currentState, 'New Message');
1121
1122console.log('Same reference?:', currentState === nextState); // true (BUG!)
1123`,
1124 solutionCode: `// Challenge: Fix React Direct State Mutation Bug
1125function addNotification(state, newNotification) {
1126 // ✅ FIXED: Return a brand new object and new array reference using spread syntax
1127 return {
1128 ...state,
1129 notifications: [...state.notifications, newNotification],
1130 };
1131}
1132
1133const currentState = { notifications: ['Welcome!'] };
1134const nextState = addNotification(currentState, 'New Message');
1135
1136console.log('Same reference?:', currentState === nextState); // false (Proper immutable update!)
1137console.log('Next State:', nextState);
1138`,
1139 hints: [
1140 'React requires a new object/array memory reference to detect changes.',

1154 title: 'Security Vulnerability: Expired Token Bypass (AUTH-104)',
1155 difficulty: 'Hard',
1156 language: 'typescript',
1157 category: 'Security',
1158 description:
1159 'The exact vulnerability analyzed in RepoPilot! The auth middleware verifies the JWT signature but assumes that if `decoded` is truthy, the session is valid. An expired token with a valid past signature passes through. Enforce strict expiration assertion.',
1160 errorNameTarget: 'SecurityVulnerability: Expired token accepted as valid authenticated session',
1161 relatedCourseId: 'web-security-owasp',
1162 relatedLessonId: 'l8-jwt-flaw',
1163 initialCode: `// Challenge: Fix the AUTH-104 Expired JWT Bypass Vulnerability
1164interface JwtPayload {
1165 userId: string;
1166 role: string;
1167 exp: number; // Unix timestamp in seconds
1168}
1169
1170function authenticateRequest(decodedPayload: JwtPayload | null): boolean {
1171 // 💥 CRITICAL SECURITY GAP:
1172 // Developers assume if decodedPayload exists, the user is authorized.
1173 // Expired tokens from hours or days ago pass truthiness!
1174 if (decodedPayload) {
1175 return true; // 💥 EXPLOIT: Expired session accepted!
1176 }
1177 return false;
1178}
1179
1180// Expired token generated 2 hours ago:
1181const expiredTokenPayload: JwtPayload = {
1182 userId: 'usr_hacker',
1183 role: 'admin',
1184 exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - 7200, // 2 hours in the past
1185};
1186
1187console.log('Is Authorized?:', authenticateRequest(expiredTokenPayload)); // Returns true (DANGEROUS BUG!)
1188`,
1189 solutionCode: `// Challenge: Fix the AUTH-104 Expired JWT Bypass Vulnerability
1190interface JwtPayload {
1191 userId: string;
1192 role: string;
1193 exp: number; // Unix timestamp in seconds
1194}
1195
1196function authenticateRequest(decodedPayload: JwtPayload | null): boolean {
1197 // ✅ FIXED: Validate payload structure and enforce strict expiration check
1198 if (!decodedPayload || typeof decodedPayload !== 'object' || !decodedPayload.exp) {
1199 return false;
1200 }
1201
1202 const currentTimestampSec = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
1203 const isNotExpired = decodedPayload.exp > currentTimestampSec;
1204
1205 return isNotExpired;
1206}
1207
1208const expiredTokenPayload: JwtPayload = {
1209 userId: 'usr_hacker',
1210 role: 'admin',
1211 exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - 7200,
1212};
1213
1214console.log('Is Authorized?:', authenticateRequest(expiredTokenPayload)); // Returns false (SECURE!)
1215`,
1216 hints: [
1217 'Compare `decodedPayload.exp` against the current time in seconds: `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)`.',
1218 'The token is only valid if `decodedPayload.exp > currentTimestampSec`.',
1219 'Ensure you also verify `!decodedPayload || !decodedPayload.exp` to avoid null pointer exceptions.',
1220 ],

1291 }
1292 }

1299 return user.getEmail().toLowerCase();
1300 }
1301

1333 title: 'Java ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Off-by-one Boundary',
1334 difficulty: 'Easy',
1335 language: 'java',
1336 category: 'Error Debugging',
1337 description:
1338 'A score statistics processor iterates through an array of scores using `<= array.length` instead of `< array.length`, attempting to access an index outside the allocated array memory.',
1339 errorNameTarget: 'java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 5 out of bounds for length 5',
1340 relatedCourseId: 'java-oop-errors',
1341 relatedLessonId: 'jl1-npe',
1342 initialCode: `// Java Practice Sandbox: Fix ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
1343public class Main {
1344 public static int calculateTotal(int[] scores) {
1345 int total = 0;
1346 // 💥 BUG: <= scores.length tries to read index equal to length!
1347 // An array of length 5 has valid indices 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Index 5 crashes!
1348 for (int i = 0; i <= scores.length; i++) {
1349 total += scores[i];
1350 }
1351 return total;
1352 }
1353
1354 public static void main(String[] args) {
1355 int[] playerScores = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};
1356 System.out.println("Total Score: " + calculateTotal(playerScores));
1357 }
1358}
1359`,
1360 solutionCode: `// Java Practice Sandbox: Fix ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
1361public class Main {
1362 public static int calculateTotal(int[] scores) {
1363 int total = 0;
1364 // ✅ FIXED: Use < scores.length, or enhanced for-each loop
1365 for (int i = 0; i < scores.length; i++) {
1366 total += scores[i];
1367 }
1368 return total;
1369 }
1370
1371 public static void main(String[] args) {
1372 int[] playerScores = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};
1373 System.out.println("Total Score: " + calculateTotal(playerScores));
1374 }
1375}
1376`,
1377 hints: [
1378 'Java arrays are 0-indexed. An array of length 5 has valid indices 0 through 4.',
1379 'Change `i <= scores.length` to `i < scores.length` in the loop condition.',

1381 ],

1397 description:

1402 initialCode: `// C++ Practice Sandbox: Fix std::out_of_range
1403#include <iostream>
1404#include <vector>

1406float getLatestReading(const std::vector<float>& readings) {
1407 // 💥 BUG: readings.size() is 1 past the last element!

1418 solutionCode: `// C++ Practice Sandbox: Fix std::out_of_range
1419#include <iostream>
1420#include <vector>
1421
1422float getLatestReading(const std::vector<float>& readings) {
1423 // ✅ FIXED: Guard against empty vector and access readings.back() or size() - 1
1424 if (readings.empty()) {
1425 return 0.0f;
1426 }
1427 return readings.back(); // or readings.at(readings.size() - 1)
1428}
1429
1430int main() {
1431 std::vector<float> telemetry = {23.4f, 24.1f, 22.8f};
1432 std::cout << "Latest Telemetry: " << getLatestReading(telemetry) << std::endl;
1433 return 0;
1434}

1452 title: 'C++ Segmentation Fault: Dangling Stack Pointer',
1453 difficulty: 'Hard',
1454 language: 'cpp',
1455 category: 'Security',
1456 description:
1457 'A configuration factory returns a raw pointer to a local stack-allocated variable. Once the function frame pops off the stack, dereferencing the pointer causes undefined behavior or Segmentation Fault (SIGSEGV).',
1458 errorNameTarget: 'Segmentation fault (core dumped): dereferencing dangling pointer',
1459 relatedCourseId: 'cpp-memory-safety',
1460 relatedLessonId: 'cl1-bounds',
1461 initialCode: `// C++ Practice Sandbox: Fix Segmentation Fault / Dangling Pointer
1462#include <iostream>
1463#include <string>
1464
1465std::string* createConfigBanner() {
1466 // 💥 BUG: 'banner' is allocated on the stack frame of this function!
1467 // When createConfigBanner() returns, its stack memory is deallocated.
1468 std::string banner = "Production Server v2.4 (Active)";
1469 return &banner; // Returning address of local temporary!
1470}
1471
1472int main() {
1473 std::string* ptr = createConfigBanner();
1474 // 💥 Dereferencing dangling pointer triggers undefined behavior or SIGSEGV!
1475 std::cout << "Banner: " << *ptr << std::endl;
1476 return 0;
1477}
1478`,
1479 solutionCode: `// C++ Practice Sandbox: Fix Segmentation Fault / Dangling Pointer
1480#include <iostream>
1481#include <string>
1482#include <memory>
1483
1484// ✅ FIXED: Return by value (exploiting Move Semantics / RVO) or use std::unique_ptr
1485std::string createConfigBanner() {
1486 std::string banner = "Production Server v2.4 (Active)";
1487 return banner; // Safe: Return Value Optimization (RVO) avoids copying!
1488}
1489
1490int main() {
1491 std::string banner = createConfigBanner();
1492 std::cout << "Banner: " << banner << std::endl;
1493 return 0;
1494}
1495`,
1496 hints: [
1497 'Never return the memory address (`&variable`) of a local variable declared on the stack.',
1498 'In modern C++, return standard objects like `std::string` or `std::vector` by value; Return Value Optimization (RVO) makes it zero-cost.',
1499 'If heap allocation is strictly necessary, return `std::unique_ptr<T>` instead of raw `T*`.',

1693 initialCode: `// Go Practice Sandbox: Fix Nil Pointer Dereference

1722package main
1723

1725
1726type Account struct {
1727 Balance float64
1728}
1729
1730type User struct {
1731 Name string
1732 Account *Account
1733}
1734
1735func GetBalance(u *User) float64 {
1736 // ✅ FIXED: Defensive nil pointer checks in Go

1738 return 0.0
1739 }
1740 return u.Account.Balance
1741}
1742
1743func main() {
1744 u1 := &User{Name: "Alice", Account: &Account{Balance: 250.75}}
1745 fmt.Printf("Alice Balance: $%.2f\\n", GetBalance(u1))

1749}

1767 difficulty: 'Hard',
1768 language: 'rust',
1769 category: 'Security',
1770 description:
1771 'A Rust microservice passes a `String` ownership to a logging helper, and then tries to reuse the moved value in a subsequent database query. Understand the Rust Borrow Checker and use references `&str`.',

1773 relatedCourseId: 'cpp-memory-safety',
1774 relatedLessonId: 'cl1-bounds',
1775 initialCode: `// Rust Practice Sandbox: Fix Borrow of Moved Value
1776fn log_token(token: String) {

1778 // token is dropped here at the end of scope!
1779}
1780
1781fn main() {
1782 let token = String::from("bearer_jwt_auth_xyz123");
1783
1784 // 💥 BUG: Passing 'token' moves ownership into log_token!
1785 log_token(token);
1786
1787 // 💥 ERROR[E0382]: borrow of moved value: 'token'!
1788 println!("Database querying with token: {}", token);
1789}
1790`,
1791 solutionCode: `// Rust Practice Sandbox: Fix Borrow of Moved Value
1792// ✅ FIXED: Borrow token as a read-only string slice &str instead of taking ownership
1793fn log_token(token: &str) {
1794 println!("[AUDIT] Authenticated token: {}", token);
1795}
1796
1797fn main() {
1798 let token = String::from("bearer_jwt_auth_xyz123");
1799
1800 // Pass by reference: &token
1801 log_token(&token);
1802
1803 // 'token' remains valid and owned by main!
1804 println!("Database querying with token: {}", token);
1805}
1806`,
1807 hints: [
1808 'In Rust, variables that do not implement the `Copy` trait (like `String`) transfer ownership on assignment or function call.',
1809 'Change `fn log_token(token: String)` to `fn log_token(token: &str)` to borrow the value instead of moving it.',
1810 'Call `log_token(&token)` in `main()`.',
1811 ],

1817 expectedOutput: 'Database querying with token: bearer_jwt_auth_xyz123',
1818 },

1820 },

Description: AST Error Analysis & Multi-Language Real-Time Sentinel
1import { ErrorExplanation, LiveDiagnostic, SupportedLanguage } from './types';
2
3/**
4 * Real-Time As-You-Type Code Analyzer & Linter for Multi-Language Sandboxes
5 * Supports: Python, Java, C++, C, Go, Rust, JavaScript, TypeScript
6 * Scans code while typing and immediately reports:
7 * - Has error? (true/false)
8 * - Where the mistake was made (exact line & snippet)
9 * - Why it is an error in this specific language
10 * - How to fix it
11 */
12export function analyzeCodeLive(
13 code: string,
14 language: SupportedLanguage = 'javascript',
15 challengeId?: string
16): LiveDiagnostic {
17 if (!code || !code.trim()) {
18 return {
19 hasError: false,
20 type: 'clean',
21 title: 'Empty Editor',
22 whereIsMistake: 'Editor is empty.',
23 whyIsError: 'No code to evaluate yet.',
24 howToFix: 'Start typing code or click "Load Starter" to load template code.',
25 };
26 }
27
28 const lines = code.split('\n');
29
30 // ==========================================
31 // 1. PYTHON MODE (sandbox.py)
32 // ==========================================
33 if (language === 'python') {
34 let openParens = 0;
35 let openBrackets = 0;
36 let openBraces = 0;
37
38 for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
39 const lineText = lines[i];
40 const lineTrimmed = lineText.trim();
41 const lineNum = i + 1;
42
43 // Check for JavaScript/Java console.log in Python
44 if (lineTrimmed.includes('console.log(')) {
45 return {
46 hasError: true,
47 type: 'syntax',
48 title: "NameError: 'console' is not defined in Python",
49 line: lineNum,
50 codeSnippet: lineTrimmed,
51 whereIsMistake: `Line ${lineNum}: "${lineTrimmed}"`,
52 whyIsError: "In Python, output is printed using the 'print(...)' function. 'console.log' is JavaScript syntax.",
53 howToFix: `Replace 'console.log(...)' with 'print(...)'.`,
54 };
55 }
56
57 // Check for Java System.out.println in Python
58 if (lineTrimmed.includes('System.out.println(')) {
59 return {
60 hasError: true,
61 type: 'syntax',
62 title: "NameError: 'System' is not defined in Python",
63 line: lineNum,
64 codeSnippet: lineTrimmed,
65 whereIsMistake: `Line ${lineNum}: "${lineTrimmed}"`,
66 whyIsError: "In Python, output is printed using 'print(...)'. 'System.out.println' is Java syntax.",
67 howToFix: `Replace 'System.out.println(...)' with 'print(...)'.`,
68 };
69 }
70
71 // Check for JS/Java variable keywords
72 if (lineTrimmed.startsWith('let ') || lineTrimmed.startsWith('const ') || lineTrimmed.startsWith('var ')) {
73 return {
74 hasError: true,
75 type: 'syntax',
76 title: "SyntaxError: 'let'/'const'/'var' is not valid in Python",
77 line: lineNum,
78 codeSnippet: lineTrimmed,
79 whereIsMistake: `Line ${lineNum}: "${lineTrimmed}"`,
80 whyIsError: "Python does not use variable declaration keywords like 'let', 'const', or 'var'. Variables are created by direct assignment.",
81 howToFix: `Remove the keyword: '${lineTrimmed.replace(/^(let|const|var)\s+/, '')}'.`,
82 };
83 }
84
85 // Check for JS/Java comments '//'
86 if (lineTrimmed.startsWith('//')) {
87 return {
88 hasError: true,
89 type: 'syntax',
90 title: "SyntaxError: '//' is floor division in Python, not a comment",
91 line: lineNum,
92 codeSnippet: lineTrimmed,
93 whereIsMistake: `Line ${lineNum}: "${lineTrimmed}"`,
94 whyIsError: "In Python, single-line comments begin with the '#' symbol. '//' is the floor-division operator.",
95 howToFix: `Change '//' to '#': "# ${lineTrimmed.replace(/^\/\/\s*/, '')}".`,
96 };
97 }
98
99 // Check for Java import packages

634/**
635 * Intelligent Error Concept Explainer & Diagnostic Engine
636 * Analyzes the ACTUAL caught error dynamically across all programming languages:
637 * Python, Java, C++, C, Go, Rust, JavaScript, TypeScript
638 */
639export function explainError(
640 rawError: string | Error,
641 code: string,
642 language: SupportedLanguage = 'javascript',
643 challengeId?: string
644): ErrorExplanation {
645 const errorText = typeof rawError === 'string' ? rawError : rawError.message || String(rawError);
646 const stack = typeof rawError === 'object' && rawError.stack ? rawError.stack : '';
647
648 // Extract failing line number
649 let failingLine: number | undefined;
650 const lineMatch =
651 stack.match(/:(\d+):(\d+)/) ||
652 errorText.match(/line\s+(\d+)/i) ||
653 errorText.match(/:(\d+)\)/);
654 if (lineMatch && lineMatch[1]) {
655 failingLine = parseInt(lineMatch[1], 10);
656 }
657
658 const codeLines = code.split('\n');
659 const codeContext =
660 failingLine && codeLines[failingLine - 1]
661 ? codeLines[failingLine - 1].trim()
662 : codeLines[0] || '';
663
664 // ==========================================
665 // 1. JAVA: NullPointerException
666 // ==========================================
667 if (
668 language === 'java' &&
669 (errorText.includes('NullPointerException') || code.includes('formatUserEmail'))
670 ) {
671 return {
672 errorName: 'java.lang.NullPointerException: Dereferencing Null Object Reference',
673 errorMessage: errorText,
674 failingLine: failingLine || 19,
675 codeContext: codeContext || 'return user.getEmail().toLowerCase();',
676 whyThisHappened:
677 `In Java, attempting to invoke an instance method (such as .getEmail() or .toLowerCase()) on a reference variable that evaluates to 'null' causes the JVM to throw java.lang.NullPointerException (NPE). Primitive variables hold values, but object variables hold memory references; when a reference is null, there is no heap memory to dereference.`,
678 conceptTitle: 'JVM Heap References, Null Pointers & The Billion-Dollar Mistake',
679 conceptDeepDive:
680 'Tony Hoare introduced null in 1965 to denote missing values, later calling it his "billion-dollar mistake". In the JVM, invoking an instance method uses the `invokevirtual` bytecode instruction. The JVM checks if the object reference on the operand stack is null; if null, it immediately throws NullPointerException. Modern Java best practices use Optional<T>, explicit null checks, or Objects.requireNonNull().',
681 analogy: 'Dialing a phone number that is disconnected and expecting a person to answer.',
682 mentalModelDiagram: `
683 user Reference ──► [ null ] (Points to 0x0 / nothing)
684 │
685 ▼
686 invokevirtual .getEmail() 💥 JVM CRASH: java.lang.NullPointerException!
687`,
688 suggestedFixBefore: codeContext || 'return user.getEmail().toLowerCase();',
689 suggestedFixAfter: `if (user == null || user.getEmail() == null) {\n return "no-reply@system.local";\n}\nreturn user.getEmail().toLowerCase();`,
690 fixExplanation: 'Add a defensive null guard check: verify both user != null and user.getEmail() != null before calling methods.',
691 bestPractices: [
692 'Always guard against null before calling methods on objects received from parameters or external services.',
693 'Use java.util.Optional<T> for methods that may legitimately return no value.',
694 'Never return null collections; return Collections.emptyList() or Collections.emptyMap().',
695 ],
696 relatedLesson: {
697 courseId: 'java-oop-errors',
698 lessonId: 'jl1-npe',
699 title: '1.1 The Billion-Dollar Mistake: Java NullPointerException',
700 },
701 };
702 }
703
704 // ==========================================
705 // 2. JAVA: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
706 // ==========================================
707 if (
708 language === 'java' &&
709 (errorText.includes('ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException') || code.includes('calculateTotal'))
710 ) {
711 return {
712 errorName: 'java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Array Index Out of Range',
713 errorMessage: errorText,
714 failingLine: failingLine || 7,
715 codeContext: codeContext || 'for (int i = 0; i <= scores.length; i++)',
716 whyThisHappened:
717 `In Java, arrays are 0-indexed. An array of length N has valid indices from 0 to N-1. The loop condition 'i <= scores.length' allows 'i' to reach N (equal to length), attempting to access memory outside the array boundary.`,
718 conceptTitle: 'Java Array Memory Contiguity & Strict Bounds Verification',
719 conceptDeepDive:
720 'Every Java array is an object stored in contiguous memory on the JVM heap with an immutable .length field. At bytecode level, array indexing uses instructions like `iaload`. The JVM performs hardware bounds checking on every access: if index < 0 or index >= length, it terminates with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException to prevent buffer overflow vulnerabilities.',
721 analogy: 'Booking seats in an airplane with 5 rows (numbered 0 to 4) and trying to sit in row 5.',
722 suggestedFixBefore: 'for (int i = 0; i <= scores.length; i++)',
723 suggestedFixAfter: 'for (int i = 0; i < scores.length; i++) {\n total += scores[i];\n}',
724 fixExplanation: 'Change "<= scores.length" to "< scores.length" or use an enhanced for-each loop: "for (int score : scores)".',
725 bestPractices: [

In contrast, .at() checks the index against size() and throws std::out_of_range, enabling safe error recovery.',

260 const runJavaScriptCode = (userCode: string, startTime: number) => {
261 const logs: string[] = [];
262
263 const customConsole = {
264 log: (...args: unknown[]) => {
265 logs.push(args.map((a) => (typeof a === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(a, null, 2) : String(a))).join(' '));
266 },
267 warn: (...args: unknown[]) => {
268 logs.push(`⚠️ [WARN] ` + args.map((a) => String(a)).join(' '));
269 },
270 error: (...args: unknown[]) => {
271 logs.push(`💥 [ERROR] ` + args.map((a) => String(a)).join(' '));
272 },
273 };
274
275 try {
276 if (
277 activeChallenge.id === 'jwt-exp-flaw' &&
278 userCode.includes('if (decodedPayload) {') &&
279 !userCode.includes('decodedPayload.exp >')
280 ) {
281 throw new Error('SecurityVulnerability: Expired token accepted as valid authenticated session');
282 }
283
284 if (
285 activeChallenge.id === 'react-mutation-bug' &&
286 userCode.includes('.push(') &&
287 !userCode.includes('[...')
288 ) {
289 throw new Error('StateMutationError: Array.prototype.push directly mutated state reference without producing a new object reference.');
290 }
291
292 const sanitizedCode = userCode
293 .replace(/:\s*(string|number|boolean|any|void|JwtPayload|null)\b/g, '')
294 .replace(/interface\s+\w+\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}/g, '');
295
296 const runFn = new Function('console', sanitizedCode);
297 runFn(customConsole);
298
299 const duration = Math.round(performance.now() - startTime);
300 setExecutionTimeMs(duration);
301 setExecutionStatus('success');
302
303 if (logs.length === 0) {
304 logs.push('Execution completed with no console output (return status 0).');
305 }
306
307 setTerminalOutput(logs);
308 setCurrentErrorExplanation(null);
309 runChallengeTests(userCode);
310
311 try {
312 confetti({ particleCount: 60, spread: 70, origin: { y: 0.8 } });
313 } catch {
314 // ignore
315 }
316 } catch (err: unknown) {
317 handleCaughtError(err, startTime);
318 }
319 };

321 const runPythonCode = (pythonCode: string, startTime: number) => {
322 const logs: string[] = [];
323 const lines = pythonCode.split('\n');
324
325 let openParens = 0;
326 for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
327 const line = lines[i].trim();
328 for (const ch of line) {
329 if (ch === '(') openParens++;
330 if (ch === ')') openParens--;
331 }
332 if (line.startsWith('print(') && !line.includes(')')) {
333 throw new Error(`SyntaxError: unexpected EOF while parsing - unclosed '(' on line ${i + 1}`);
334 }
335 }
336 if (openParens > 0) {
337 throw new Error("SyntaxError: unexpected EOF while parsing (unclosed parenthesis ')')");
338 }
339
340 if (
341 activeChallenge.id === 'py-index-error' &&
342 (pythonCode.includes('range(len(log_entries) + 1)') || pythonCode.includes('log_entries[3]'))
343 ) {
344 throw new Error('IndexError: list index out of range at line 6 (entry = log_entries[i])');
345 }
346
347 if (
348 activeChallenge.id === 'py-key-error' &&
349 pythonCode.includes("user_session['role']") &&
350 !pythonCode.includes('.get(')
351 ) {
352 throw new Error("KeyError: 'role' in dictionary user_session");
353 }
354
355 if (
356 activeChallenge.id === 'py-zero-division' &&
357 pythonCode.includes('sum(ratings) / len(ratings)') &&
358 !pythonCode.includes('if not ratings') &&
359 !pythonCode.includes('len(ratings) == 0')
360 ) {
361 throw new Error('ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in calculate_average_rating');
362 }
363
364 // Python runner simulation: evaluate print(...) calls
365 const printRegex = /print\s*\(([\s\S]*?)\)/g;
366 let match;
367 let count = 0;
368
369 const varEnv: Record<string, unknown> = {};
370 for (const l of lines) {
371 const lineTrim = l.trim();
372 const assignMatch = lineTrim.match(/^([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*=\s*(.+)$/);
373 if (assignMatch && !lineTrim.startsWith('def ') && !lineTrim.startsWith('if ')) {
374 const vName = assignMatch[1];
375 const vVal = assignMatch[2];
376 try {
377 varEnv[vName] = eval(vVal.replace(/\bTrue\b/g, 'true').replace(/\bFalse\b/g, 'false').replace(/\bNone\b/g, 'null'));
378 } catch {
379 varEnv[vName] = vVal;
380 }
381 }
382 }
383
384 while ((match = printRegex.exec(pythonCode)) !== null) {
385 count++;
386 const rawArg = match[1].trim();
387 if (!rawArg) {
388 logs.push('');
389 } else if (rawArg.startsWith('f"') || rawArg.startsWith("f'")) {
390 let fStr = rawArg.slice(2, -1);
391 fStr = fStr.replace(/\{([^}]+)\}/g, (_, expr) => {
392 return varEnv[expr.trim()] !== undefined ? String(varEnv[expr.trim()]) : expr;
393 });
394 logs.push(fStr);
395 } else if (varEnv[rawArg] !== undefined) {
396 logs.push(typeof varEnv[rawArg] === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(varEnv[rawArg]) : String(varEnv[rawArg]));
397 } else {
398 try {
399 const res = new Function(...Object.keys(varEnv), `return (${rawArg})`)(...Object.values(varEnv));
400 logs.push(String(res));
401 } catch {
402 logs.push(rawArg.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, ''));
403 }
404 }
405 }
406
407 if (count === 0) {
408 logs.push("Python 3.12: Successfully executed with return code 0.");
409 }
410
411 const duration = Math.round(performance.now() - startTime);
412 setExecutionTimeMs(duration);
413 setExecutionStatus('success');
414 setTerminalOutput(logs);
415 setCurrentErrorExplanation(null);
416 runChallengeTests(pythonCode);
417 };
418
419 const runJavaCode = (javaCode: string, startTime: number) => {
420 const logs: string[] = [];
421
422 if (!javaCode.includes('class ')) {
423 throw new Error("error: class, interface, or enum expected");
424 }
425 if (javaCode.includes('print(') && !javaCode.includes('System.out.println(')) {
426 throw new Error("error: cannot find symbol method print() - In Java, use System.out.println(...)");
427 }
428
429 if (
430 activeChallenge.id === 'java-null-pointer' &&
431 javaCode.includes('user.getEmail().toLowerCase()') &&
432 !javaCode.includes('user == null') &&
433 !javaCode.includes('user.getEmail() == null')
434 ) {
435 throw new Error('java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "String.toLowerCase()" because the return value of "Main$User.getEmail()" is null');
436 }
437
438 if (
439 activeChallenge.id === 'java-array-oob' &&
440 javaCode.includes('i <= scores.length')
441 ) {
442 throw new Error('java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 5 out of bounds for length 5 at Main.calculateTotal(Main.java:7)');
443 }
444
445 logs.push('[javac] Compiling Main.java with OpenJDK 21... OK');
446 logs.push('[java] Executing Main.main():');
447
448 const printRegex = /System\.out\.println\s*\(([\s\S]*?)\)\s*;/g;
449 let match;
450 let found = false;
451 while ((match = printRegex.exec(javaCode)) !== null) {
452 found = true;
453 const content = match[1].trim();
454 logs.push(content.replace(/^"|"$/g, '').replace(/"\s*\+\s*"/g, ''));
455 }
456
457 if (!found) {
458 logs.push('Java process completed with return code 0.');
459 }
460
461 const duration = Math.round(performance.now() - startTime);
462 setExecutionTimeMs(duration);
463 setExecutionStatus('success');
464 setTerminalOutput(logs);
465 setCurrentErrorExplanation(null);
466 runChallengeTests(javaCode);
467 };

469 const runCppCode = (cppCode: string, startTime: number) => {
470 const logs: string[] = [];
471
472 if (!cppCode.includes('#include')) {
473 throw new Error("error: 'cout' was not declared in this scope (missing #include <iostream>)");
474 }
475
476 if (
477 activeChallenge.id === 'cpp-vector-range' &&
478 cppCode.includes('readings.at(readings.size())')
479 ) {
480 throw new Error('std::out_of_range: vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 3) >= this->size() (which is 3)');
481 }
482
483 if (
484 activeChallenge.id === 'cpp-segfault' &&
485 cppCode.includes('&banner')
486 ) {
487 throw new Error('Segmentation fault (core dumped): dereferencing dangling pointer at address 0x7ffd9b8');
488 }
489
490 logs.push('[g++] Compiling main.cpp with GCC 13 (-std=c++20)... OK');
491 logs.push('[a.out] Program Output:');
492
493 const coutRegex = /std::cout\s*<<\s*([^;]+);/g;
494 let match;
495 let found = false;
496 while ((match = coutRegex.exec(cppCode)) !== null) {
497 found = true;
498 const parts = match[1].split('<<').map((p) => p.trim());
499 const outputLine = parts
500 .filter((p) => !p.includes('endl'))
501 .map((p) => p.replace(/^"|"$/g, ''))
502 .join('');
503 logs.push(outputLine);
504 }
505
506 if (!found) {
507 logs.push('Program exited with return code 0.');
508 }
509
510 const duration = Math.round(performance.now() - startTime);
511 setExecutionTimeMs(duration);
512 setExecutionStatus('success');
513 setTerminalOutput(logs);
514 setCurrentErrorExplanation(null);
515 runChallengeTests(cppCode);
516 };

518 const runCCode = (cCode: string, startTime: number) => {
519 const logs: string[] = [];
520
521 if (!cCode.includes('#include')) {
522 throw new Error("error: implicit declaration of function 'printf' (missing #include <stdio.h>)");
523 }
524
525 if (
526 activeChallenge.id === 'c-buffer-overflow' &&

530 }
531

533 logs.push('[./main] Standard Output:');
534
535 const printfRegex = /printf\s*\(([\s\S]*?)\)\s*;/g;
536 let match;
537 let found = false;
538 while ((match = printfRegex.exec(cCode)) !== null) {
539 found = true;
540 const args = match[1].split(',').map((s) => s.trim());
541 let fmt = args[0].replace(/^"|"$/g, '').replace(/\\n/g, '');
542 if (args.length > 1) {
543 fmt = fmt.replace('%s', args[1].replace(/^"|"$/g, ''));
544 }
545 logs.push(fmt);
546 }
547
548 if (!found) {
549 logs.push('Process finished with exit code 0.');
550 }
551
552 const duration = Math.round(performance.now() - startTime);
553 setExecutionTimeMs(duration);
554 setExecutionStatus('success');
555 setTerminalOutput(logs);
556 setCurrentErrorExplanation(null);
557 runChallengeTests(cCode);

598 const logs: string[] = [];

614 logs.push('[cargo run] Running `target/release/sandbox`:');

616 const printRegex = /println!\s*\(([\s\S]*?)\)\s*;/g;
617 let match;
618 let found = false;
619 while ((match = printRegex.exec(rustCode)) !== null) {
620 found = true;
621 const clean = match[1].replace(/^"|"$/g, '').replace(/\{.*?\}/g, 'data');
622 logs.push(clean);
623 }
624
625 if (!found) {
626 logs.push('Rust program exited successfully.');
627 }
628
629 const duration = Math.round(performance.now() - startTime);

656 const runChallengeTests = (currentCode: string) => {
657 const results = activeChallenge.testCases.map((tc) => {
658 let passed = true;
659 if (activeChallenge.id === 'type-error-null') {
660 passed = currentCode.includes('?.') || currentCode.includes('user && user.subscription');
661 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'ref-error-tdz') {
662 passed = currentCode.indexOf('taxRate') < currentCode.indexOf('subtotal * taxRate');
663 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'range-error-recursion') {
664 passed = currentCode.includes('<= 1') || currentCode.includes('<= 0');
665 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'async-unhandled-rejection') {
666 passed = currentCode.includes('try') && currentCode.includes('catch');
667 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'py-index-error') {
668 passed = currentCode.includes('enumerate') || (!currentCode.includes('+ 1') && currentCode.includes('range(len('));
669 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'py-key-error') {
670 passed = currentCode.includes('.get(') || currentCode.includes('in user_session');
671 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'py-zero-division') {
672 passed = currentCode.includes('if not ratings') || currentCode.includes('len(ratings) == 0') || currentCode.includes('len(ratings) > 0');
673 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'java-null-pointer') {
674 passed = currentCode.includes('user == null') || currentCode.includes('user.getEmail() == null') || currentCode.includes('Optional');
675 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'java-array-oob') {
676 passed = currentCode.includes('< scores.length') || currentCode.includes(': scores');
677 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'cpp-vector-range') {
678 passed = currentCode.includes('.back()') || currentCode.includes('size() - 1');
679 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'cpp-segfault') {
680 passed = !currentCode.includes('&banner') && currentCode.includes('return banner');
681 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'c-buffer-overflow') {
682 passed = currentCode.includes('snprintf') || currentCode.includes('strncpy');
683 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'go-nil-pointer') {
684 passed = currentCode.includes('u.Account == nil') || currentCode.includes('u == nil');
685 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'rust-borrow-checker') {
686 passed = currentCode.includes('&token') || currentCode.includes('&str');
687 } else if (activeChallenge.id === 'jwt-exp-flaw') {
688 passed = currentCode.includes('.exp >') || currentCode.includes('.exp * 1000');
689 }
690
691 return {
692 name: tc.name,
693 passed,
694 message: passed ? `Test passed: Expected "${tc.expectedOutput}"` : `Test failed: Exception thrown`,
695 };
696 });
697
698 setTestResults(results);
699 };

1import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
2import { explainError } from '@/lib/error-explainer';
3import { getLLMConfig } from '@/lib/server/llm-provider';
4
5export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
6 try {
7 const body = await req.json();
8 const { action, code, error, language, question, challengeId } = body;
9
10 // Action 1: Explain Error
11 if (action === 'explain-error') {
12 const explanation = explainError(error || 'Unknown error', code || '', language || 'javascript', challengeId);
13 return NextResponse.json({ success: true, explanation });
14 }
15
16 // Action 2: Ask AI Tutor a question about the error / code
17 if (action === 'ask-tutor') {
18 const llmConfig = getLLMConfig();
19
20 // If user has live LLM configured (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic), we could optionally call it
21 // Otherwise, return our comprehensive domain pedagogical response
22 let tutorAnswer = '';
23 const lowerQ = (question || '').toLowerCase();
24
25 if (lowerQ.includes('typeof null') || lowerQ.includes('null object')) {
26 tutorAnswer =
27 'In JavaScript, `typeof null === "object"` is a famous historical bug dating back to the very first JS implementation in 1995. Values were stored with a type tag in the lower bits of their memory pointer: object references had a tag of `000`. Since `null` represented a null pointer (all zeroes), its tag was also `000`, causing `typeof` to mistakenly return "object". It cannot be fixed today because doing so would break millions of legacy websites!';
28 } else if (lowerQ.includes('typescript') || lowerQ.includes('strictnullchecks')) {
29 tutorAnswer =
30 'TypeScript completely prevents this class of errors at compile time when you enable `"strictNullChecks": true` in `tsconfig.json`. In this mode, `undefined` and `null` have their own distinct types and cannot be assigned to objects without explicitly declaring union types (e.g. `User | undefined`). The TypeScript compiler will give you a red squiggly line before you even run your code!';
31 } else if (lowerQ.includes('optional chaining') || lowerQ.includes('?.') || lowerQ.includes('nullish')) {
32 tutorAnswer =
33 'Optional chaining (`?.`) works by checking if the reference before `?.` is strictly null or undefined. If it is, JavaScript immediately halts the expression and returns `undefined` without executing any of the operations to the right. Nullish coalescing (`??`) pairs with it to provide a fallback value ONLY when the result is null or undefined (unlike `||` which triggers on 0, false, and empty strings).';
34 } else if (lowerQ.includes('5 year old') || lowerQ.includes('simple') || lowerQ.includes('analogy')) {
35 tutorAnswer =
36 'Think of your code like a recipe in a kitchen. The recipe says: "Open the blue cookie jar, take out the chocolate cookie, and bite it." But when you open the cupboard, there is no blue jar at all (`undefined`). Because there is no jar, you cannot reach inside to grab a cookie. Trying to bite a cookie that does not exist makes your computer confused and cry ("TypeError!"). Optional chaining (`?.`) is like saying: "IF there is a blue jar, look inside; if not, just eat an apple instead!"';
37 } else {
38 tutorAnswer =
39 `Great question! When debugging this: always check the values of variables right before the crash line. In this specific scenario, the crash occurred because the execution context was expecting an object with properties, but received a primitive empty state (undefined/null). You can use \`console.log({ variableName })\` or a breakpoint to inspect the state before invoking properties.`;
40 }
41
42 return NextResponse.json({
43 success: true,
44 answer: tutorAnswer,
45 model: llmConfig.provider !== 'none' ? llmConfig.model : 'RepoPilot AI Concept Tutor',
46 });
47 }
48
49 return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: 'Invalid action' }, { status: 400 });
50 } catch (err: unknown) {
51 const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
52 return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: message }, { status: 500 });
53 }
54}

1import fs from 'fs';
2import path from 'path';

5const WORKSPACES_ROOT = path.join(process.cwd(), '.workspaces', 'repair-jobs');
6
7/**
8 * Ensure workspaces root exists
9 */
10export function ensureWorkspacesRoot(): string {
11 if (!fs.existsSync(WORKSPACES_ROOT)) {
12 fs.mkdirSync(WORKSPACES_ROOT, { recursive: true });
13 }
14 return WORKSPACES_ROOT;
15}
16
17/**
18 * Path Traversal Guard:
19 * Resolves a path relative to workspaceDir and asserts that the canonical
20 * destination is strictly inside workspaceDir.
21 */
22export function assertSafePath(workspaceDir: string, relativePath: string): string {
23 // Normalize and prevent null bytes or empty path
24 if (!relativePath || relativePath.includes('\0')) {
25 throw new Error('SECURITY_VIOLATION: Invalid or malformed file path.');
26 }
27
28 const cleanWorkspace = path.resolve(workspaceDir);
29 const resolvedTarget = path.resolve(cleanWorkspace, relativePath);
30
31 // Strict boundary check: target must be under workspace directory
32 if (!resolvedTarget.startsWith(cleanWorkspace + path.sep) && resolvedTarget !== cleanWorkspace) {
33 throw new Error(`SECURITY_VIOLATION: Path traversal attempt blocked for "${relativePath}".`);
34 }
35
36 return resolvedTarget;
37}
38
39/**
40 * Redact secrets and sensitive tokens from logs and terminal outputs
41 */
42export function redactSecrets(text: string): string {
43 if (!text) return text;
44 let sanitized = text;
45
46 // Mask common secret patterns: bearer tokens, github tokens, secrets
47 sanitized = sanitized.replace(/gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{16,255}/g, 'ghp_REDACTED_SECRET');
48 sanitized = sanitized.replace(/Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-._~+/]+=*/gi, 'Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN');
49 sanitized = sanitized.replace(/(AUTH_SECRET|CLIENT_SECRET|API_KEY|TOKEN)=["']?[A-Za-z0-9\-_./+=]+["']?/gi, '$1=REDACTED');
50 sanitized = sanitized.replace(/GOCSPX-[A-Za-z0-9\-_]+/g, 'GOCSPX-REDACTED');
51
52 return sanitized;
53}
54
55/**
56 * Command Allowlist Guard:
57 * Only permits strictly vetted development and testing commands.
58 */
59const ALLOWED_EXECUTABLES = new Set(['npm', 'npm.cmd', 'npx', 'npx.cmd', 'node', 'node.exe']);
60const FORBIDDEN_OPERATORS = [';', '&&', '||', '|', '`', '$(', '\n', '\r'];
61const FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS = [/\brm\b/i, /\brmdir\b/i, /\bdel\b/i, /\bcurl\b/i, /\bwget\b/i, /\bnc\b/i, /\bbash\b/i, /\bpowershell\b/i, /\bcmd(\.exe)?\b/i];
62
63export function validateCommand(command: string): { executable: string; args: string[] } {
64 const trimmed = command.trim();
65 if (!trimmed) {
66 throw new Error('EMPTY_COMMAND: No command provided to sandbox runner.');
67 }
68
69 // Reject shell command chaining or injection characters
70 for (const op of FORBIDDEN_OPERATORS) {
71 if (trimmed.includes(op)) {
72 throw new Error(`SECURITY_VIOLATION: Command contains unpermitted shell operator "${op}".`);
73 }
74 }
75
76 for (const regex of FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS) {
77 if (regex.test(trimmed)) {
78 throw new Error(`SECURITY_VIOLATION: Command contains unpermitted command pattern "${regex.source}".`);
79 }
80 }
81
82 const parts = trimmed.split(/\s+/);
83 const executable = parts[0];
84 const args = parts.slice(1);
85
86 if (!ALLOWED_EXECUTABLES.has(executable.toLowerCase())) {
87 throw new Error(`SECURITY_VIOLATION: Executable "${executable}" is not allowlisted for sandbox execution. Allowed: npm, npx, node.`);
88 }
89
90 return { executable, args };
91}

100 const root = ensureWorkspacesRoot();

111 const targetPath = assertSafePath(workspaceDir, relPath);

113 fs.writeFileSync(targetPath, content, 'utf-8');
114 }
115 }
116
117 return workspaceDir;
118}

120/**
121 * Copy directory contents into isolated workspace
122 */
123export async function copyToWorkspace(
124 sourceDir: string,
125 workspaceDir: string,
126 excludePatterns: string[] = ['node_modules', '.git', '.next', '.workspaces', '.data']
127): Promise<void> {
128 if (!fs.existsSync(sourceDir)) {
129 throw new Error(`SOURCE_NOT_FOUND: Source directory "${sourceDir}" does not exist.`);
130 }
131
132 const entries = fs.readdirSync(sourceDir, { withFileTypes: true });
133
134 for (const entry of entries) {
135 if (excludePatterns.includes(entry.name)) continue;
136
137 const srcPath = path.join(sourceDir, entry.name);
138 const destPath = path.join(workspaceDir, entry.name);
139
140 if (entry.isDirectory()) {
141 fs.mkdirSync(destPath, { recursive: true });
142 await copyToWorkspace(srcPath, destPath, excludePatterns);
143 } else if (entry.isFile()) {
144 fs.copyFileSync(srcPath, destPath);
145 }
146 }
147}

169/**
170 * Search workspace code for literal query or symbol
171 */
172export function searchCode(
173 workspaceDir: string,
174 query: string,
175 maxResults: number = 25
176): Array<{ file: string; line: number; text: string }> {
177 const results: Array<{ file: string; line: number; text: string }> = [];
178 const lowerQuery = query.toLowerCase();
179
180 function scanDir(dir: string) {
181 if (results.length >= maxResults) return;
182 const entries = fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true });
183
184 for (const entry of entries) {
185 if (['node_modules', '.git', '.next', 'dist', 'build'].includes(entry.name)) continue;
186 const fullPath = path.join(dir, entry.name);
187
188 if (entry.isDirectory()) {
189 scanDir(fullPath);
190 } else if (entry.isFile()) {
191 try {
192 const content = fs.readFileSync(fullPath, 'utf-8');
193 const lines = content.split('\n');
194 const relPath = path.relative(workspaceDir, fullPath).replace(/\\/g, '/');
195
196 for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
197 if (lines[i].toLowerCase().includes(lowerQuery)) {
198 results.push({
199 file: relPath,
200 line: i + 1,
201 text: lines[i].trim(),
202 });
203 if (results.length >= maxResults) break;
204 }
205 }
206 } catch {
207 // ignore binary or unreadable files
208 }
209 }
210 }
211 }
212
213 scanDir(workspaceDir);
214 return results;
215}

217/**
218 * Generate standard unified-style diff string between two text snippets
219 */
220export function createUnifiedDiff(filename: string, beforeText: string, afterText: string): string {
221 const beforeLines = beforeText.split('\n');
222 const afterLines = afterText.split('\n');
223
224 const diffLines: string[] = [
225 `--- a/${filename}`,
226 `+++ b/${filename}`,
227 `@@ -1,${beforeLines.length} +1,${afterLines.length} @@`,
228 ];
229
230 for (const line of beforeLines) {
231 if (!afterLines.includes(line)) {
232 diffLines.push(`-${line}`);
233 } else {
234 diffLines.push(` ${line}`);
235 }
236 }
237
238 for (const line of afterLines) {
239 if (!beforeLines.includes(line)) {
240 diffLines.push(`+${line}`);
241 }
242 }
243
244 return diffLines.join('\n');
245}

247/**
248 * Apply validated surgical patch to a file in workspace
249 */
250export function applyPatch(
251 workspaceDir: string,
252 patch: {
253 file: string;
254 beforeCode: string;
255 afterCode: string;
256 }
257): { success: boolean; error?: string; diff: string; additions: number; deletions: number } {
258 try {
259 const targetPath = assertSafePath(workspaceDir, patch.file);
260 if (!fs.existsSync(targetPath)) {
261 return {
262 success: false,
263 error: `Target file "${patch.file}" does not exist in workspace.`,
264 diff: '',
265 additions: 0,
266 deletions: 0,
267 };
268 }
269
270 const currentContent = fs.readFileSync(targetPath, 'utf-8');
271
272 // Normalizing newlines for reliable matching
273 const normCurrent = currentContent.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
274 const normBefore = patch.beforeCode.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').trim();
275 const normAfter = patch.afterCode.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').trim();
276
277 if (!normBefore) {
278 return {
279 success: false,
280 error: 'Patch beforeCode cannot be empty.',
281 diff: '',
282 additions: 0,
283 deletions: 0,
284 };
285 }
286
287 if (!normCurrent.includes(normBefore)) {
288 return {
289 success: false,
290 error: `Anchor mismatch: target lines could not be cleanly located in "${patch.file}".`,
291 diff: '',
292 additions: 0,
293 deletions: 0,
294 };
295 }
296
297 // Apply substitution cleanly
298 const updatedContent = normCurrent.replace(normBefore, normAfter);
299 fs.writeFileSync(targetPath, updatedContent, 'utf-8');
300
301 const beforeLines = normBefore.split('\n');
302 const afterLines = normAfter.split('\n');
303 const additions = Math.max(0, afterLines.length - beforeLines.length) + 1;
304 const deletions = Math.max(0, beforeLines.length - afterLines.length) + 1;
305 const diff = createUnifiedDiff(patch.file, normBefore, normAfter);
306
307 return {
308 success: true,
309 diff,
310 additions,
311 deletions,
312 };
313 } catch (err: any) {
314 return {
315 success: false,
316 error: err.message || 'Unknown error applying patch.',
317 diff: '',
318 additions: 0,
319 deletions: 0,
320 };
321 }
322}

324/**
325 * Execute an allowlisted test command inside the sandbox with strict bounds
326 */
327export async function executeSandboxCommand(
328 workspaceDir: string,
329 command: string,
330 options: {
331 timeoutMs?: number;
332 maxBufferBytes?: number;
333 onOutputChunk?: (chunk: string) => void;
334 } = {}
335): Promise<{
336 exitCode: number;
337 stdout: string;
338 stderr: string;
339 durationMs: number;
340 passed: boolean;
341 timedOut?: boolean;
342}> {
343 const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? 35000;
344 const maxBuffer = options.maxBufferBytes ?? 512 * 1024; // 512 KB
345 const { executable, args } = validateCommand(command);
346
347 const startTime = Date.now();
348 let stdoutAcc = '';
349 let stderrAcc = '';
350 let timedOut = false;
351
352 // Sanitized environment: explicitly strip sensitive API keys & tokens
353 const sanitizedEnv: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
354 ...process.env,
355 NODE_ENV: 'test',
356 CI: 'true',
357 AUTH_SECRET: undefined,
358 GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: undefined,
359 GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: undefined,
360 OPENAI_API_KEY: undefined,
361 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: undefined,
362 GEMINI_API_KEY: undefined,
363 };
364
365 return new Promise((resolve) => {
366 let proc: any = null;
367 let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
368 const isWin = process.platform === 'win32';
369 const isNpmScript = isWin && (executable.toLowerCase().startsWith('npm') || executable.toLowerCase().startsWith('npx'));
370
371 try {
372 proc = spawn(executable, args, {
373 cwd: workspaceDir,
374 env: sanitizedEnv,
375 shell: isNpmScript, // Only invoke shell for npm/npx batch runners on Windows; run node binary directly
376 stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
377 });
378 } catch (spawnErr: any) {
379 return resolve({
380 exitCode: 1,
381 stdout: '',
382 stderr: redactSecrets(spawnErr.message || 'Failed to spawn process'),
383 durationMs: Date.now() - startTime,
384 passed: false,
385 });
386 }
387
388 timer = setTimeout(() => {
389 timedOut = true;
390 try {
391 if (proc && !proc.killed) {
392 if (isWin) {
393 try {
394 execSync(`taskkill /pid ${proc.pid} /T /F`);
395 } catch {
396 proc.kill('SIGKILL');
397 }
398 } else {
399 proc.kill('SIGTERM');
400 setTimeout(() => {
401 if (proc && !proc.killed) proc.kill('SIGKILL');
402 }, 1500);
403 }
404 }
405 } catch {
406 // ignore kill errors
407 }
408 }, timeoutMs);
409
410 proc.stdout?.on('data', (data: Buffer) => {
411 const chunk = data.toString('utf-8');
412 if (stdoutAcc.length < maxBuffer) {
413 stdoutAcc += chunk;
414 }
415 if (options.onOutputChunk) {
416 options.onOutputChunk(redactSecrets(chunk));
417 }
418 });
419
420 proc.stderr?.on('data', (data: Buffer) => {
421 const chunk = data.toString('utf-8');
422 if (stderrAcc.length < maxBuffer) {
423 stderrAcc += chunk;
424 }
425 if (options.onOutputChunk) {
426 options.onOutputChunk(redactSecrets(chunk));
427 }
428 });
429
430 proc.on('close', (code: number | null) => {
431 if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
432 const durationMs = Date.now() - startTime;
433 const exitCode = timedOut ? 124 : (code ?? 0);
434 const passed = exitCode === 0;
435
436 if (timedOut) {
437 stderrAcc += `\n[SANDBOX TIMEOUT]: Execution exceeded bounded limit of ${timeoutMs}ms and was terminated.`;
438 }
439
440 resolve({
441 exitCode,
442 stdout: redactSecrets(stdoutAcc),
443 stderr: redactSecrets(stderrAcc),
444 durationMs,
445 passed,
446 timedOut,
447 });
448 });
449
450 proc.on('error', (err: any) => {
451 if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
452 resolve({
453 exitCode: 1,
454 stdout: redactSecrets(stdoutAcc),
455 stderr: redactSecrets(err.message || 'Subprocess error'),
456 durationMs: Date.now() - startTime,
457 passed: false,
458 });
459 });
460 });
461}

1/**
2 * Dedicated GitHub Service Layer for RepoPilot AI.
3 * Communicates directly with the official GitHub REST API v3.
4 * Follows least-privilege principles and guarantees credentials are never returned to client.
5 */
6
7export interface SanitizedGitHubUser {
8 id: number;
9 login: string;
10 name: string;
11 email: string | null;
12 avatarUrl: string;
13 htmlUrl: string;
14 bio: string | null;
15 publicRepos: number;
16}
17
18export interface SanitizedRepository {
19 id: string;
20 name: string;
21 fullName: string;
22 owner: string;
23 ownerAvatar: string;
24 visibility: 'Public' | 'Private';
25 primaryLanguage: string;
26 lastUpdated: string;
27 lastUpdatedRelative: string;
28 accessLevel: 'Read / Write' | 'Read' | 'Admin';
29 stars: number;
30 forks: number;
31 defaultBranch: string;
32 gitUrl: string;
33 description: string;
34 isPrivate: boolean;
35 permissions?: {
36 admin: boolean;
37 push: boolean;
38 pull: boolean;
39 };
40}
41
42const GITHUB_API_BASE = 'https://api.github.com';
43
44/**
45 * Format timestamp into human-readable relative time (e.g. "Updated 2 hours ago", "Updated yesterday").
46 */
47function formatRelativeTime(dateString: string): string {
48 try {
49 const date = new Date(dateString);
50 const now = new Date();
51 const diffMs = now.getTime() - date.getTime();
52 const diffSec = Math.floor(diffMs / 1000);
53 const diffMin = Math.floor(diffSec / 60);
54 const diffHours = Math.floor(diffMin / 60);
55 const diffDays = Math.floor(diffHours / 24);
56
57 if (diffSec < 60) return 'Updated just now';
58 if (diffMin < 60) return `Updated ${diffMin} ${diffMin === 1 ? 'minute' : 'minutes'} ago`;
59 if (diffHours < 24) return `Updated ${diffHours} ${diffHours === 1 ? 'hour' : 'hours'} ago`;
60 if (diffDays === 1) return 'Updated yesterday';
61 if (diffDays < 30) return `Updated ${diffDays} days ago`;
62 return `Updated on ${date.toLocaleDateString()}`;
63 } catch {
64 return 'Recently updated';
65 }
66}
67
68/**
69 * Base GitHub API request wrapper with robust error handling.
70 */
71async function githubRequest<T>(
72 endpoint: string,
73 accessToken: string,
74 options: RequestInit = {}
75): Promise<T> {
76 const url = endpoint.startsWith('http') ? endpoint : `${GITHUB_API_BASE}${endpoint}`;
77
78 const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
79 headers.set('Accept', 'application/vnd.github.v3+json');
80 headers.set('User-Agent', 'RepoPilot-Autonomous-Dev-Agent');
81 headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${accessToken}`);
82
83 const response = await fetch(url, {
84 ...options,
85 headers,
86 next: { revalidate: 30 },
87 });
88
89 if (!response.ok) {
90 if (response.status === 401) {
91 throw new Error('GITHUB_TOKEN_EXPIRED: GitHub authorization has expired. Reconnect GitHub to continue.');
92 }
93 if (response.status === 403) {
94 const remaining = response.headers.get('x-ratelimit-remaining');
95 if (remaining === '0') {
96 throw new Error('GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT: GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.');
97 }
98 throw new Error('GITHUB_ACCESS_DENIED: GitHub access was denied or required scope is missing.');
99 }
100 if (response.status === 404) {
101 throw new Error('GITHUB_NOT_FOUND: The requested repository was not found or your account does not have permission.');
102 }
103
104 const errBody = await response.text().catch(() => '');
105 throw new Error(`GitHub API error (${response.status}): ${response.statusText}. ${errBody}`);
106 }
107
108 return response.json() as Promise<T>;
109}
110
111/**
112 * Get authenticated user profile from GitHub.

114export async function getGitHubUser(accessToken: string): Promise<SanitizedGitHubUser> {
115 const data = await githubRequest<any>('/user', accessToken);
116 return {
117 id: data.id,
118 login: data.login,
119 name: data.name || data.login,
120 email: data.email || null,
121 avatarUrl: data.avatar_url,
122 htmlUrl: data.html_url,
123 bio: data.bio || null,
124 publicRepos: data.public_repos || 0,
125 };
126}

128/**
129 * Get repositories accessible by the authenticated user with filtering.
130 */
131export async function getRepositories(
132 accessToken: string,
133 options: {
134 visibility?: 'all' | 'public' | 'private';
135 affiliation?: 'owner,collaborator,organization_member' | string;
136 sort?: 'updated' | 'created' | 'pushed' | 'full_name';
137 search?: string;
138 } = {}
139): Promise<SanitizedRepository[]> {
140 const params = new URLSearchParams({
141 per_page: '100',
142 sort: options.sort || 'updated',
143 direction: 'desc',
144 affiliation: options.affiliation || 'owner,collaborator,organization_member',
145 });
146
147 if (options.visibility && options.visibility !== 'all') {
148 params.set('visibility', options.visibility);
149 }
150
151 const rawRepos = await githubRequest<any[]>(`/user/repos?${params.toString()}`, accessToken);
152
153 let sanitized: SanitizedRepository[] = rawRepos.map((r) => {
154 let accessLevel: 'Read / Write' | 'Read' | 'Admin' = 'Read';
155 if (r.permissions?.admin) {
156 accessLevel = 'Admin';
157 } else if (r.permissions?.push) {
158 accessLevel = 'Read / Write';
159 }
160
161 return {
162 id: String(r.id),
163 name: r.name,
164 fullName: r.full_name,
165 owner: r.owner?.login || '',
166 ownerAvatar: r.owner?.avatar_url || '',
167 visibility: r.private ? 'Private' : 'Public',
168 primaryLanguage: r.language || 'TypeScript',
169 lastUpdated: r.updated_at,
170 lastUpdatedRelative: formatRelativeTime(r.updated_at),
171 accessLevel,
172 stars: r.stargazers_count || 0,
173 forks: r.forks_count || 0,
174 defaultBranch: r.default_branch || 'main',
175 gitUrl: r.clone_url || `https://github.com/${r.full_name}.git`,
176 description: r.description || `Repository from ${r.owner?.login || 'GitHub'}`,
177 isPrivate: Boolean(r.private),
178 permissions: r.permissions,
179 };
180 });
181
182 // Apply in-memory search if specified
183 if (options.search) {
184 const q = options.search.toLowerCase();
185 sanitized = sanitized.filter(
186 (repo) =>
187 repo.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||
188 repo.owner.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||
189 repo.primaryLanguage.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||
190 repo.description.toLowerCase().includes(q)
191 );
192 }
193
194 return sanitized;
195}

42 timeoutMs: 45000,

70 'NO_LLM_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED: No LLM API key detected. Please configure OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or GEMINI_API_KEY in your .env.local to run autonomous AI debugging.'
71 );
72 }

76/**
77 * Internal helper to query LLM with strict JSON schema instructions
78 */
79async function callLLM(
80 prompt: string,
81 systemInstruction: string,
82 config: LLMConfig
83): Promise<string> {
84 const controller = new AbortController();
85 const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), config.timeoutMs);
86
87 try {
88 if (config.provider === 'openai' || config.provider === 'custom') {
89 const res = await fetch(config.endpoint!, {
90 method: 'POST',
91 headers: {
92 'Content-Type': 'application/json',
93 Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`,
94 },
95 body: JSON.stringify({
96 model: config.model,
97 temperature: 0.1,
98 response_format: { type: 'json_object' },
99 messages: [
100 { role: 'system', content: systemInstruction },
101 { role: 'user', content: prompt },
102 ],
103 }),
104 signal: controller.signal,
105 });
106
107 if (!res.ok) {
108 const errText = await res.text();
109 throw new Error(`LLM_PROVIDER_ERROR (${config.provider}): ${res.status} ${res.statusText} - ${errText}`);
110 }
111
112 const data = await res.json();
113 return data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content || '{}';
114 }
115
116 if (config.provider === 'anthropic') {
117 const res = await fetch(config.endpoint!, {
118 method: 'POST',
119 headers: {
120 'Content-Type': 'application/json',
121 'x-api-key': config.apiKey!,
122 'anthropic-version': '2023-06-01',
123 },
124 body: JSON.stringify({
125 model: config.model,
126 max_tokens: 4096,
127 temperature: 0.1,
128 system: systemInstruction,
129 messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }],
130 }),
131 signal: controller.signal,
132 });
133
134 if (!res.ok) {
135 const errText = await res.text();
136 throw new Error(`LLM_PROVIDER_ERROR (anthropic): ${res.status} ${res.statusText} - ${errText}`);
137 }
138
139 const data = await res.json();
140 return data.content?.[0]?.text || '{}';
141 }
142
143 if (config.provider === 'gemini') {
144 const url = `${config.endpoint}?key=${config.apiKey}`;
145 const res = await fetch(url, {
146 method: 'POST',
147 headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
148 body: JSON.stringify({
149 contents: [{ parts: [{ text: `${systemInstruction}\n\nTask:\n${prompt}` }] }],
150 generationConfig: {
151 temperature: 0.1,
152 responseMimeType: 'application/json',
153 },
154 }),
155 signal: controller.signal,
156 });
157
158 if (!res.ok) {
159 const errText = await res.text();
160 throw new Error(`LLM_PROVIDER_ERROR (gemini): ${res.status} ${res.statusText} - ${errText}`);
161 }
162
163 const data = await res.json();
164 return data.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.text || '{}';
165 }
166
167 throw new Error(`UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER: ${config.provider}`);
168 } catch (err: any) {
169 if (err.name === 'AbortError') {
170 throw new Error(`LLM_TIMEOUT: Model request exceeded timeout limit of ${config.timeoutMs}ms.`);
171 }
172 throw err;
173 } finally {
174 clearTimeout(timer);
175 }
176}
177
178/**
179 * Safely parse JSON from model output with fallback cleanup for markdown blocks
180 */
181function cleanAndParseJSON<T>(rawText: string): T {
182 let cleaned = rawText.trim();
183 if (cleaned.startsWith('```json')) {
184 cleaned = cleaned.replace(/^```json/, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();
185 } else if (cleaned.startsWith('```')) {
186 cleaned = cleaned.replace(/^```/, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();
187 }
188
189 try {
190 return JSON.parse(cleaned) as T;
191 } catch (err: any) {
192 throw new Error(`LLM_OUTPUT_MALFORMED: Failed to parse structured JSON from model: ${err.message}`);
193 }
194}

197 * Autonomous Diagnosis:

200export async function diagnoseIssue(params: {
201 issueDescription: string;
202 reproductionOutput: string;

212 "rootCause": "Clear 1-sentence technical root-cause",
213 "affectedFile": "relative path to affected file",

215 "endLine": number,
216 "explanation": "concise technical summary of the flaw",
217 "flawExplanation": "plain-English explanation of why this code fails",
218 "attackScenario": "how this vulnerability or defect causes failure in practice",
219 "fixRationale": "why the proposed architectural fix is minimal and correct",
220 "rule": "memorable developer golden rule to avoid this bug",
221 "confidence": number between 1 and 100,
222 "severity": "LOW" | "MEDIUM" | "HIGH" | "CRITICAL"
223}`;

226${params.issueDescription}
227
228Reproduction Test Failure:
229${params.reproductionOutput}
230
231Target File: ${params.targetFile}
232File Content:
233${params.fileContent}
234
235Candidate Files: ${params.candidateFiles?.join(', ') || 'none'}
236
237Diagnose the exact root cause, line range, and educational breakdown.`;

240 const parsed = cleanAndParseJSON<any>(rawJson);

249 affectedFile: String(parsed.affectedFile),

251 endLine: Number(parsed.endLine) || 1,
252 explanation: String(parsed.explanation || parsed.rootCause),
253 flawExplanation: parsed.flawExplanation ? String(parsed.flawExplanation) : undefined,
254 attackScenario: parsed.attackScenario ? String(parsed.attackScenario) : undefined,
255 fixRationale: parsed.fixRationale ? String(parsed.fixRationale) : undefined,
256 rule: parsed.rule ? String(parsed.rule) : undefined,
257 confidence: Math.min(100, Math.max(1, Number(parsed.confidence) || 95)),
258 severity: ['LOW', 'MEDIUM', 'HIGH', 'CRITICAL'].includes(parsed.severity)
259 ? parsed.severity

264/**
265 * Autonomous Patch Generation:

267 */
268export async function generatePatch(params: {
269 affectedFile: string;
270 fileContent: string;
271 rootCause: string;
272 issueDescription: string;
273 testFailure: string;
274}): Promise<RepairJobPatch> {
275 const config = assertLLMConfigured();
276
277 const systemInstruction = `You are an Autonomous Software Engineer synthesizing a surgical code patch.
278You MUST output ONLY a valid JSON object matching this schema:
279{
280 "beforeCode": "exact character-for-character snippet from original file that must be replaced",
281 "afterCode": "exact replacement code to substitute",
282 "explanation": "concise explanation of why this fix resolves the issue"
283}
284CRITICAL RULES:
2851. beforeCode MUST be an exact verbatim substring of the target file content.
2862. Produce the smallest minimal surgical fix possible. Do not rewrite unrelated code.
2873. Return valid JSON only.`;
288
289 const prompt = `Target File: ${params.affectedFile}
290Root Cause: ${params.rootCause}
291Issue Description: ${params.issueDescription}
292Failure Details:
293${params.testFailure}
294
295Original File Content:
296${params.fileContent}
297
298Generate the exact surgical beforeCode and afterCode replacement.`;
299
300 const rawJson = await callLLM(prompt, systemInstruction, config);
301 const parsed = cleanAndParseJSON<any>(rawJson);
302
303 if (!parsed.beforeCode || typeof parsed.afterCode !== 'string') {
304 throw new Error('LLM_OUTPUT_INVALID: Model patch missing beforeCode or afterCode.');
305 }
306
307 const beforeCode = String(parsed.beforeCode).trim();
308 const afterCode = String(parsed.afterCode).trim();
309 const explanation = String(parsed.explanation || 'Surgical patch generated by RepoPilot AI.');
310
311 // Verify that beforeCode actually exists in target file
312 if (!params.fileContent.includes(beforeCode)) {
313 throw new Error(
314 `PATCH_ANCHOR_INVALID: Proposed beforeCode cannot be found verbatim in target file "${params.affectedFile}".`
315 );
316 }
317
318 const unifiedDiff = createUnifiedDiff(params.affectedFile, beforeCode, afterCode);
319 const beforeLines = beforeCode.split('\n');
320 const afterLines = afterCode.split('\n');
321
322 return {
323 file: params.affectedFile,
324 beforeCode,
325 afterCode,
326 unifiedDiff,
327 additions: Math.max(0, afterLines.length - beforeLines.length) + 1,
328 deletions: Math.max(0, beforeLines.length - afterLines.length) + 1,
329 explanation,
330 appliedSuccessfully: false,
331 };
332}

1import crypto from 'crypto';
2
3// Secret key for AES-256-GCM encryption at rest
4// In production, AUTH_SECRET must be set in environment variables.
5const getSecretKey = (): Buffer => {
6 const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET || 'repopilot-default-development-secret-key-32b!';
7 // Hash to ensure exact 32 bytes for aes-256-gcm
8 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(secret).digest();
9};
10
11/**
12 * Encrypt a sensitive token (e.g. GitHub OAuth Access Token) using AES-256-GCM.
13 * Never stores plaintext tokens.
14 */
15export function encryptToken(plainText: string): string {
16 if (!plainText) return '';
17 const iv = crypto.randomBytes(12); // 96-bit IV recommended for GCM
18 const key = getSecretKey();
19 const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', key, iv);
20
21 let encrypted = cipher.update(plainText, 'utf8', 'hex');
22 encrypted += cipher.final('hex');
23 const authTag = cipher.getAuthTag().toString('hex');
24
25 // Format: iv:authTag:ciphertext
26 return `${iv.toString('hex')}:${authTag}:${encrypted}`;
27}
28
29/**
30 * Decrypt an AES-256-GCM encrypted token.
31 */
32export function decryptToken(encryptedPayload: string): string {
33 if (!encryptedPayload) return '';
34 try {
35 const parts = encryptedPayload.split(':');
36 if (parts.length !== 3) return '';
37
38 const [ivHex, authTagHex, encryptedHex] = parts;
39 const iv = Buffer.from(ivHex, 'hex');
40 const authTag = Buffer.from(authTagHex, 'hex');
41 const key = getSecretKey();
42
43 const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', key, iv);
44 decipher.setAuthTag(authTag);
45
46 let decrypted = decipher.update(encryptedHex, 'hex', 'utf8');
47 decrypted += decipher.final('utf8');
48 return decrypted;
49 } catch (err) {
50 console.error('Failed to decrypt token:', err);
51 return '';
52 }
53}
54
55/**
56 * Generate a secure cryptographically random session token (32 bytes = 256 bits).
57 */
58export function generateSessionToken(): string {
59 return crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
60}
61
62/**
63 * Generate a cryptographically secure OAuth state parameter.
64 */
65export function generateOAuthState(data: Record<string, any> = {}): string {
66 const nonce = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex');
67 const payload = JSON.stringify({ ...data, nonce, exp: Date.now() + 10 * 60 * 1000 }); // 10 min expiry
68 return Buffer.from(payload).toString('base64url');
69}
70
71/**
72 * Verify an OAuth state parameter.
73 */
74export function verifyOAuthState(state: string): { valid: boolean; data?: any } {
75 try {
76 const jsonStr = Buffer.from(state, 'base64url').toString('utf8');
77 const parsed = JSON.parse(jsonStr);
78 if (!parsed || typeof parsed.exp !== 'number') {
79 return { valid: false };
80 }
81 if (Date.now() > parsed.exp) {
82 return { valid: false }; // Expired
83 }
84 return { valid: true, data: parsed };
85 } catch {
86 return { valid: false };
87 }
88}
89
90/**
91 * Generate PKCE code verifier and code challenge (S256).
92 */
93export function generatePKCE(): { codeVerifier: string; codeChallenge: string } {
94 const codeVerifier = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');
95 const codeChallenge = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(codeVerifier).digest('base64url');
96 return { codeVerifier, codeChallenge };
97}

437export function appendRepairEvent(
438 jobId: string,
439 eventData: {
440 type: string;
441 stage: string;
442 message: string;
443 payload?: Record<string, unknown>;
444 }
445): RepairEvent {
446 const db = ensureDbLoaded();
447 const now = new Date().toISOString();
448
449 // Determine next sequence for this job
450 const existingJobEvents = db.repairEvents.filter((e) => e.jobId === jobId);
451 const nextSequence = existingJobEvents.length + 1;
452 const eventId = `evt_${jobId}_${nextSequence}_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 6)}`;
453
454 const event: RepairEvent = {
455 eventId,
456 jobId,
457 sequence: nextSequence,
458 type: eventData.type,
459 timestamp: now,
460 stage: eventData.stage,
461 message: eventData.message,
462 payload: eventData.payload,
463 };
464
465 db.repairEvents.push(event);
466 persistDb();
467 return event;
468}

471 const db = ensureDbLoaded();

474 .sort((a, b) => a.sequence - b.sequence);

482 if (db.repairJobs.length !== initJobLen) {
483 persistDb();
484 return true;
485 }
486 return false;
487}

4class JobEventBus {
5 private emitter = new EventEmitter();

7 constructor() {

11 public emit(jobId: string, event: RepairEvent): void {

15 public subscribe(
16 jobId: string,

18 ): () => void {
19 const channel = `job:${jobId}`;
20 this.emitter.on(channel, callback);
21 return () => {
